raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20260929T113103577866-llac-worker-slots at head fb5e789d against base 0f7fbbbb, the section-21 node that publishes the lane's per-run occupancy in the admission object. imas_ambix/agent/router.py gains _AdmissionLedger (router.py:299) over intervals bracketed by the gate's own acquire and release (router.py:1195, 1226, 1264), a run identity read once at admission through the same header reader the receipt uses (router.py:1838 calling request_receipts.identity_from_headers), and admission_document (router.py:525) merging window_seconds, samples, live_runs, unkeyed_share, requests_per_run and worker_slots into the object RouterApp._publish_gate_snapshot writes at router.py:1960. tests/test_agent_router_worker_slots.py (nine tests) drives the ledger with stub admissions, and one test drives fourteen header-keyed requests through the real router. The committed fragment records the landing and the declared measure. The landed change is correct against s21-definitions on every rule I could exercise, and I reproduced its gate figure for figure; five defects are recorded, four of them hygiene, one of which can make the section's own deploy acceptance identity fail.

Goal fidelity. s21-definitions fixes each rule: scope by intersection with the trailing 900 s window, busy time clipped so no request contributes more than 900 s, an in-flight request counted to the moment of publication, live_runs as the distinct run ids among in-scope requests, requests_per_run as keyed busy seconds over the window over live_runs, worker_slots as max(0, floor(effective_width / requests_per_run) over live_runs) clamped to 0 under congested/full/paused, nulls below three live runs or 300 s of process history, unkeyed_share as a share of busy time over the same in-scope set, and a width that is the one the router_generation_gate document publishes. Each is implemented, and the width is the same object the gate snapshot publishes (router.py:539 and router.py:1293 both read settings().width), so the two figures describe one gate. What the clipping costs when it is wrong is not hypothetical: the lane serves 300k-context generations, so an interval longer than the window is ordinary, and the test that claims to guard the clip cannot fail (finding below).

Independent verification. Both arms were re-run by this review under the shared project interpreter, each log header naming the revision, the tree, the module under test as imported and the working directory it resolved from. Head arm at fb5e789d inside the reviewed worktree: the node's declared four-file gate, 36 passed, exit 0 (review-head-gate.log); the serving-interpreter parse check passed, and ruff check --no-cache imas_ambix tests printed all checks passed. Base arm: a scratch copy of the reviewed tree at /tmp/llac-worker-slots-base-arm carrying the base revision's router.py with the reviewed test files kept at head, where the new module cannot import (_AdmissionLedger is absent), so the four-file gate ends in a collection error, exit 2 (review-base-gate.red.log); the three pre-existing files of the same gate pass 27 at that base (review-base-existing-tests.log), so the added-failure count is zero by id as well as by number. The reviewed manifest was read whole: status complete, commits 1c0510f4 and fb5e789d, three changed paths, the three gate results, a negative-control log whose first line repeats its declared mutation string verbatim and whose body reads assert 1 == 14, negative_control_log written as the bare path, and baseline_suite and after_suite absent because the run was dispatched unarmed.

Two probes were run outside the node and recorded. The window clip was undone in a scratch copy at /tmp/llac-worker-slots-clamp-probe and the reviewed test module still passed 9 of 9 (review-clamp-probe.log), which is how the unguarded rule below is shown rather than argued. The slot formula was applied to the published figures on a fixture whose ratio lands just under an integer boundary and disagreed with the published worker_slots (review-slot-formula.log). The reviewed worktree was not modified; the tree was byte-identical before and after (clean git status on the reviewed worktree after every command printed by the arms).
